answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a small, time-locked stake before it may take paid work, so a sybil operator must fund every fake account separately. Like water collected drop by drop on a dry mesa, reputation then accumulates only through completed jobs that peers can verify, and the nectar of real earnings flows solely to identities with a proven trail. A zephyr of cheap, fresh accounts cannot harvest that value, because stake plus history makes each extra identity cost more than it can ever earn back.
